King’s Lynn Rotary Club pledges support for therapy room project
The Rotary Club of King’s Lynn has promised to support a refurbishment project at the Mr Bee’s Family Centre. The pledge follows a presentation by Abbie Mulcairn from the charity Brave Futures, which provides specialist support to children and young people across Norfolk and Suffolk who have experienced sexual abuse.
During the meeting, the charity highlighted that referrals at their King’s Lynn centre have more than doubled over the past six months. Rotary club members heard that the organisation is currently managing high demand while navigating challenges within the criminal justice system. The club president confirmed they will assist with the planned improvements to the centre’s therapy room.

item.title: Harding’s Pits in South Lynn granted village green status
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Harding’s Pits in South Lynn granted village green status
A long-running campaign to protect Harding’s Pits in South Lynn has reached a successful conclusion. Norfolk County Council has officially approved the site for village green status, following a proposal submitted by West Norfolk Council earlier this year.
The designation provides statutory protection against development and encroachment, ensuring the land remains available for community use. This decision marks the end of a process spanning more than 30 years, which began with an initial application by the Lynn 2,000 lobby group. Local campaigners and councillors have welcomed the news, noting that the status will safeguard the area’s natural habitats and public open space for future generations.

Wisbech teenager to be sentenced for park knife attack
An eighteen-year-old man from Wisbech is due to be sentenced next month following a knife attack in a local park. Densias Griaitis, of The Lawns, was found guilty at Peterborough Magistrates' Court last Tuesday. He was convicted of grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon.
The charges follow an incident at Wisbech Park on August 20 last year, where a sixteen-year-old boy was wounded. Griaitis has been remanded on conditional bail and is scheduled to appear at Cambridge Crown Court for sentencing on November 17.

item.description:

Family pays tribute to Yaxley motorcyclist following fatal Sawtry collision
The family of 23-year-old Tyler Ellis from Yaxley has paid tribute to him following a fatal collision on the B1043 Old North Road at Sawtry. Mr Ellis was riding a black Kawasaki motorcycle when it collided with a red Volvo HGV at approximately 12:50pm on Monday, October 5. He passed away at Addenbrooke’s Hospital the following day.
The 76-year-old lorry driver from Wisbech was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has since been released on bail until January 4. Cambridgeshire Constabulary is continuing to appeal for witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage of the incident to come forward by calling 101 or visiting the force's website.

item.title: King’s Lynn Rotary club donates £500 to support Kolkata street children
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Rotary club donates £500 to support Kolkata street children
A King’s Lynn couple has received a £500 donation from the local Priory Rotary Club to support The Hope Foundation for Street Children. Dr Prabir Mitra and his wife Sanjukta recently completed a 111-day, 28,200-mile road journey from King’s Lynn to Kolkata.
The pair travelled through Europe, Central Asia, China, Tibet, and Nepal, crossing 20 international borders. During the trip, they raised awareness about diabetes and collected funds for a dialysis unit at The Hope Hospital in Kolkata. The Rotary donation will assist the foundation in providing education and protection for street children. The couple faced numerous challenges during their expedition, including difficult road conditions and frequent border closures.

Weasenham Lane in Wisbech closed following burst water main
Drivers in Wisbech are facing further disruption on Weasenham Lane. The road is currently closed following a burst water main that occurred over the weekend. Anglian Water has confirmed that repairs to the pipe are finished, but the route remains shut while crews work to fix the damaged road surface.
This marks the third time in four months that the road has been closed due to a burst main. Anglian Water says the closure will remain in place until it is safe for traffic to return. The company has thanked local residents for their patience while these essential repairs are completed.
